1→# UltraJSON
     2→
     3→[![PyPI version](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/ujson.svg?logo=pypi&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     4→[![Supported Python versions](https://img.shields.io/pypi/pyversions/ujson.svg?logo=python&logoColor=FFE873)](https://pypi.org/project/ujson)
     5→[![PyPI downloads](https://img.shields.io/pypi/dm/ujson.svg)](https://pypistats.org/packages/ujson)
     6→[![GitHub Actions status](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/workflows/Test/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ultrajson/ultrajson/actions)
     7→[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/ultrajson/ultrajson)
     8→[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/1418941.svg)](https://zenodo.org/badge/latestdoi/1418941)
     9→[![Code style: Black](https://img.shields.io/badge/code%20style-Black-000000.svg)](https://github.com/psf/black)
    10→
    11→UltraJSON is an ultra fast JSON encoder and decoder written in pure C with bindings for
    12→Python.
    13→
    14→Install with pip:
    15→
    16→```sh
    17→python -m pip install ujson
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Project status
    21→
    22→> [!WARNING]
    23→> UltraJSON's architecture is fundamentally ill-suited to making changes without
    24→> risk of introducing new security vulnerabilities. As a result, this library
    25→> has been put into a *maintenance-only* mode. Support for new Python versions
    26→> will be added and critical bugs and security issues will still be
    27→> fixed but all other changes will be rejected. Users are encouraged to migrate
    28→> to [orjson](https://pypi.org/project/orjson/) which is both much faster and
    29→> less likely to introduce a surprise buffer overflow vulnerability in the
    30→> future.
    31→
    32→## Usage
    33→
    34→May be used as a drop in replacement for most other JSON parsers for Python:
    35→
    36→```pycon
    37→>>> import ujson
    38→>>> ujson.dumps([{"key": "value"}, 81, True])
    39→'[{"key":"value"},81,true]'
    40→>>> ujson.loads("""[{"key": "value"}, 81, true]""")
    41→[{'key': 'value'}, 81, True]
    42→```
    43→
    44→### Encoder options
    45→
    46→#### encode_html_chars
    47→
    48→Used to enable special encoding of "unsafe" HTML characters into safer Unicode
    49→sequences. Default is `False`:
    50→
    51→```pycon
    52→>>> ujson.dumps("<script>John&Doe", encode_html_chars=True)
    53→'"\\u003cscript\\u003eJohn\\u0026Doe"'
    54→```
    55→
    56→#### ensure_ascii
    57→
    58→Limits output to ASCII and escapes all extended characters above 127. Default is `True`.
    59→If your end format supports UTF-8, setting this option to false is highly recommended to
    60→save space:
    61→
    62→```pycon
    63→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö")
    64→'"\\u00e5\\u00e4\\u00f6"'
    65→>>> ujson.dumps("åäö", ensure_ascii=False)
    66→'"åäö"'
    67→```
    68→
    69→#### escape_forward_slashes
    70→
    71→Controls whether forward slashes (`/`) are escaped. Default is `True`:
    72→
    73→```pycon
    74→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com")
    75→'"https:\\/\\/example.com"'
    76→>>> ujson.dumps("https://example.com", escape_forward_slashes=False)
    77→'"https://example.com"'
    78→```
    79→
    80→#### indent
    81→
    82→Controls whether indentation ("pretty output") is enabled. Default is `0` (disabled):
    83→
    84→```pycon
    85→>>> ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"})
    86→'{"foo":"bar"}'
    87→>>> print(ujson.dumps({"foo": "bar"}, indent=4))
    88→{
    89→    "foo": "bar"
    90→}
    91→```
    92→
    93→## Benchmarks
    94→
    95→*UltraJSON* calls/sec compared to other popular JSON parsers with performance gain
    96→specified below each.
    97→
    98→### Test machine
    99→
   100→Linux 5.15.0-1037-azure x86_64 #44-Ubuntu SMP Thu Apr 20 13:19:31 UTC 2023
   101→
   102→### Versions
   103→
   104→- CPython 3.11.3 (main, Apr  6 2023, 07:55:46) [GCC 11.3.0]
   105→- ujson        : 5.7.1.dev26
   106→- orjson       : 3.9.0
   107→- simplejson   : 3.19.1
   108→- json         : 2.0.9
   109→
   110→|                                                                               | ujson      | orjson     | simplejson | json       |

   139→Above metrics are in call/sec, larger is better.
   140→
   141→## Build options
   142→
   143→For those with particular needs, such as Linux distribution packagers, several
   144→build options are provided in the form of environment variables.
   145→
   146→### Debugging symbols
   147→
   148→#### UJSON_BUILD_NO_STRIP
   149→
   150→By default, debugging symbols are stripped on Linux platforms. Setting this
   151→environment variable with a value of `1` or `True` disables this behavior.
   152→
   153→### Using an external or system copy of the double-conversion library
   154→
   155→These two environment variables are typically used together, something like:
   156→
   157→```sh
   158→export UJSON_BUILD_DC_INCLUDES='/usr/include/double-conversion'
   159→export UJSON_BUILD_DC_LIBS='-ldouble-conversion'
   160→```
   161→
   162→Users planning to link against an external shared library should be aware of
   163→the ABI-compatibility requirements this introduces when upgrading system
   164→libraries or copying compiled wheels to other machines.
   165→
   166→#### UJSON_BUILD_DC_INCLUDES
   167→
   168→One or more directories, delimited by `os.pathsep` (same as the `PATH`
   169→environment variable), in which to look for `double-conversion` header files;
   170→the default is to use the bundled copy.
   171→
   172→#### UJSON_BUILD_DC_LIBS
   173→
   174→Compiler flags needed to link the `double-conversion` library; the default
   175→is to use the bundled copy.

    34→class FuzzGenerator:
    35→    """A random JSON serialisable object generator."""

    37→    def __init__(self, seed=None):
    38→        self._randomizer = random.Random(seed)
    39→        self._shrink = 1

    41→    def key(self):
    42→        key_types = [self.int, self.float, self.string, self.null, self.bool]
    43→        return self._randomizer.choice(key_types)()

    45→    def item(self):
    46→        if self._randomizer.random() > 0.8:

    53→    def float(self):
    54→        sign = self._randomizer.choice([-1, 1, 0])
    55→        return sign * math.exp(self._randomizer.uniform(-40, 40))
    56→
    57→    def string(self):
    58→        characters = ["\x00", "\t", "a", "\U0001f680", "<></>", "\u1234"]
    59→        return self._randomizer.choice(characters) * self.length()

    61→    def bool(self):
    62→        return self._randomizer.random() < 0.5
    63→
    64→    def null(self):

    66→
    67→    def list(self):
    68→        return [self.item() for i in range(self.length())]
    69→
    70→    def dict(self):
    71→        return {self.key(): self.item() for i in range(self.length())}

   158→def fuzz(seeds, **options):
   159→    try:

   161→            data = random_object(seed)

   163→                _options = dict(zip(options.keys(), permutation))
   164→                print(f"--seed {seed}", *(f"--{k} {v}" for (k, v) in _options.items()))

   166→                data_objects = collect_all_objects(data)
   167→                # Exclude ints because they get referenced by the lists below.
   168→                data_objects = [o for o in data_objects if not isinstance(o, int)]
   169→                gc.collect()
   170→                data_ref_counts_before = [sys.getrefcount(o) for o in data_objects]
   171→                ujson.dumps(data, **_options)
   172→                gc.collect()
   173→                data_ref_counts_after = [sys.getrefcount(o) for o in data_objects]
   174→                if data_ref_counts_before != data_ref_counts_after:
   175→                    for o, before, after in zip(
   176→                        data_objects, data_ref_counts_before, data_ref_counts_after
   177→                    ):

   179→                            print(f"Ref count of {o!r} went from {before} to {after}")

   185→def collect_all_objects(obj):
   186→    """Given an object, return a list of all objects referenced by it."""
   187→
   188→    if hasattr(sys, "pypy_version_info"):
   189→        # PyPy's GC works differently (no ref counting), so this wouldn't be useful.
   190→        # Simply returning an empty list effectively disables the refcount test.
   191→        return []
   192→
   193→    def _inner(o):
   194→        yield o
   195→        if isinstance(o, list):
   196→            for v in o:
   197→                yield from _inner(v)
   198→        elif isinstance(o, dict):
   199→            for k, v in o.items():
   200→                yield from _inner(k)
   201→                yield from _inner(v)

   203→    out = []

   205→    for o in _inner(obj):
   206→        if id(o) not in seen:
   207→            seen.add(id(o))
   208→            out.append(o)

## Detailed Analysis of UltraJSON (ujson) Library

### 1. LIBRARY OVERVIEW

**UltraJSON** is an ultra-fast JSON encoder and decoder library written in pure C with Python bindings. It provides high-performance JSON serialization and deserialization.

**Key Characteristics:**
- Implemented in C for speed (significantly faster than standard Python json module)
- Pure C implementation with Python C API bindings
- Uses the double-conversion library for float/double conversion
- Currently in **maintenance-only mode** due to security concerns with its architecture
- Supported on Python 3.10+ (CPython, PyPy, GraalPy)

### 2. MAIN PUBLIC API FUNCTIONS

The library exposes 6 primary functions (all accessible via `ujson` module):

#### **Parsing Functions (Untrusted Input)**

| Function | Module Path | Purpose |
|----------|------------|---------|
| `loads(str)` | `ujson.c:66` mapped to `JSONToObj()` in `python/JSONtoObj.c:163` | Parses JSON string into Python objects |
| `decode(str)` | `ujson.c:65` mapped to `JSONToObj()` in `python/JSONtoObj.c:163` | Alias for `loads()` |
| `load(file)` | `ujson.c:70` mapped to `JSONFileToObj()` in `python/JSONtoObj.c:288` | Parses JSON from file object |

#### **Encoding Functions**

| Function | Module Path | Purpose |
|----------|------------|---------|
| `dumps(obj, **kwargs)` | `ujson.c:67` mapped to `objToJSON()` in `python/objToJSON.c:660` | Encodes Python objects to JSON string |
| `encode(obj, **kwargs)` | `ujson.c:65` mapped to `objToJSON()` in `python/objToJSON.c:660` | Alias for `dumps()` |
| `dump(obj, file, **kwargs)` | `ujson.c:69` mapped to `objToJSONFile()` in `python/objToJSON.c:866` | Encodes Python objects to JSON file |

#### **Exception Class**

| Exception | Location | Purpose |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| `JSONDecodeError` | `ujson.c:194` | Custom exception for JSON parsing errors (inherits from `ValueError`) |

### 3. BEST FUZZING TARGETS (Parsing Untrusted Input)

The following functions are **EXCELLENT fuzzing targets** because they parse untrusted string/bytes input:

#### **Primary Fuzzing Targets**

1. **`ujson.loads()` / `ujson.decode()`**
   - Function path: `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:163` (`JSONToObj`)
   - Accepts: String or bytes-like objects
   - Calls: `JSON_DecodeObject()` at line 247
   - Processing: Converts JSON string to Python objects
   - Parser implementation: `/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c`

2. **`ujson.load()`**
   - Function path: `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c:288` (`JSONFileToObj`)
   - Accepts: File objects with `.read()` method
   - Processing: Reads from file and calls `JSONToObj()` internally
   - Fuzzing note: Can test with file-like objects

#### **Low-Level Parser Functions (C Layer)**

These internal C functions are called by `JSON_DecodeObject`:

| Function | File | Lines | What it parses |
|----------|------|-------|-----------------|
| `decode_any()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 747-788 | Entry point for all JSON values |
| `decode_string()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 362+ | JSON strings with escape sequences |
| `decode_numeric()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 91-247 | Numbers (int, long, double) |
| `decode_array()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 589-651 | JSON arrays `[...]` |
| `decode_object()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 653-745 | JSON objects `{...}` |
| `decode_true()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 249-268 | Boolean `true` |
| `decode_false()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 269-289 | Boolean `false` |
| `decode_null()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 291-310 | Null value |
| `decodeDouble()` | `ultrajsondec.c` | 78-90 | Floating point numbers using double-conversion library |
| `JSON_DecodeObject()` | `ultrajsondec.c:790` | 790-834 | Main decoder entry point |

### 4. ENCODING FUNCTIONS (Less critical but still fuzzable)

The encoder (`dumps`/`encode`) is less critical for security but still worth testing:

| Function | File | Lines | Purpose |
|----------|------|-------|---------|
| `objToJSON()` | `python/objToJSON.c` | 660-865 | Python-C interface for encoding |
| `encode()` | `lib/ultrajsonenc.c` | 665+ | Main encoding logic |
| `JSON_EncodeObject()` | `lib/ultrajsonenc.c` | 953-1000+ | C-level encoder entry point |

**Encoder parameters (fuzzing attack surface):**
- `ensure_ascii` (default: True) - escape non-ASCII
- `encode_html_chars` (default: False) - escape HTML chars
- `escape_forward_slashes` (default: True) - escape `/`
- `sort_keys` (default: False) - sort dict keys
- `indent` (default: 0) - pretty-print spacing
- `allow_nan` (default: True) - allow NaN/Infinity
- `reject_bytes` (default: True) - reject bytes objects
- `default` (default: None) - custom encoder function
- `separators` (default: None) - custom item/key separators

### 5. PACKAGE STRUCTURE

```
/app/ujson/
├── src/ujson/
│   ├── python/           # Python C API bindings
│   │   ├── ujson.c       # Module initialization & public API definitions
│   │   ├── ujson.h       # Header (minimal)
│   │   ├── JSONtoObj.c   # JSON string to Python object conversion
│   │   ├── objToJSON.c   # Python object to JSON string conversion
│   │   └── version_template.h
│   ├── lib/              # Core C encoder/decoder
│   │   ├── ultrajson.h   # Main header with type definitions
│   │   ├── ultrajsondec.c # JSON decoder (pure C)
│   │   ├── ultrajsonenc.c # JSON encoder (pure C)
│   │   └── dconv_wrapper.cc # Double-conversion library wrapper
│   └── deps/
│       └── double-conversion/ # External dependency for float parsing
├── tests/
│   ├── test_ujson.py     # Unit tests
│   ├── fuzz.py          # Existing fuzzer (tests ujson.dumps)
│   └── benchmark.py
├── setup.py             # Build configuration
├── pyproject.toml       # Project metadata
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

### 6. DEPENDENCIES

**Build Dependencies** (from `setup.py` and `pyproject.toml`):
- `setuptools>=42` - build system
- `setuptools_scm>=3.4` - version management
- `C++ compiler` - for double-conversion library compilation
- External libraries: `-lstdc++ -lm` (C++ standard library, math library)

**Runtime Dependencies:**
- Python 3.10+ (CPython, PyPy, or GraalPy)
- Compiled C extension module (`ujson` module)

**Optional:**
- `decimal` module (standard library) - for Decimal type support

**No external Python dependencies at runtime** - it's a pure compiled C extension.

### 7. CRITICAL SECURITY NOTES FOR FUZZING

From the README warning:
> UltraJSON's architecture is fundamentally ill-suited to making changes without risk of introducing new security vulnerabilities. As a result, this library has been put into a maintenance-only mode.

**Known fuzzing risk areas:**
1. **String parsing with escape sequences** - `decode_string()` handles Unicode escapes (`\uXXXX`)
2. **Numeric parsing** - uses double-conversion library, potential precision issues
3. **Nested structures** - recursion depth checking (max 1024 levels defined in `ultrajson.h:70`)
4. **Memory management** - C code with manual malloc/free
5. **Buffer overflows** - String concatenation in encoder, integer overflow in numeric parsing
6. **Stack buffer usage** - Fixed 1024-byte stack buffer for escape sequences (line 795 in `ultrajsondec.c`)

### 8. KEY DATA STRUCTURES & CONSTANTS

From `/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/ultrajson.h`:

**Important Constants:**
- `JSON_DOUBLE_MAX_DECIMALS` = 15 - max decimal places for float output
- `JSON_MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH` = 1024 - max nesting for encoder
- `JSON_MAX_OBJECT_DEPTH` = 1024 - max nesting for decoder
- `JSON_MAX_STACK_BUFFER_SIZE` = 1024 - stack buffer for escape sequences

**Data Types:**
```c
enum JSTYPES {
  JT_NULL, JT_TRUE, JT_FALSE, JT_INT, JT_LONG, JT_ULONG,
  JT_DOUBLE, JT_UTF8, JT_RAW, JT_ARRAY, JT_OBJECT,
  JT_INVALID, JT_NAN, JT_POS_INF, JT_NEG_INF
};
```

**Decoder State Structure** (`ultrajsondec.c:50`):
```c
struct DecoderState {
  char *start, *end;           // Input buffer bounds
  JSUINT32 *escStart, *escEnd; // Escape sequence buffer
  int escHeap;                 // Flag if buffer allocated on heap
  int lastType;                // Last decoded type
  JSUINT32 objDepth;           // Current nesting depth
  void *prv;                   // Private context
  JSONObjectDecoder *dec;      // Decoder callbacks
};
```

### 9. RECOMMENDED FUZZING STRATEGIES

**High-Impact Fuzzing Targets:**

1. **String Parsing (`ujson.loads()`)** with:
   - Various escape sequences (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\u0000-\uffff`)
   - Unicode edge cases (surrogates, invalid UTF-8)
   - Deeply nested arrays/objects (recursion depth)
   - Large numbers (integer overflow, precision)
   - Invalid JSON (trailing data, malformed syntax)

2. **Edge Cases:**
   - Extremely long strings
   - Maximum recursion depth (1024 levels)
   - Stack buffer overflow in escape handling
   - Invalid UTF-8 sequences
   - Numeric precision edge cases

3. **Object Encoding (`ujson.dumps()`)** with:
   - Circular reference detection (not performed!)
   - Custom `default` function callback
   - Various separator combinations
   - Deep object nesting
   - Mixed type dictionaries

### 10. FILE LOCATIONS SUMMARY

| Component | Path |
|-----------|------|
| Module definition | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/ujson.c` |
| Decoder interface | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/JSONtoObj.c` |
| Encoder interface | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c` |
| Decoder implementation | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c` |
| Encoder implementation | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c` |
| Header definitions | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/lib/ultrajson.h` |
| Python header | `/app/ujson/src/ujson/python/ujson.h` |
| Unit tests | `/app/ujson/tests/test_ujson.py` |
| Existing fuzzer | `/app/ujson/tests/fuzz.py` |
| Build config | `/app/ujson/setup.py` |
| Metadata | `/app/ujson/pyproject.toml` |

This library is an excellent target for fuzzing due to its C implementation, handling of untrusted JSON input, and known architectural security concerns. The parsing functions (`loads`, `decode`, `load`) that accept user-supplied JSON strings are the primary attack surface.
